acceptance_criteria.criterion: `ObfuscationServiceTests` defines all stub classes as `private` nested classes within the test class — no shared test-helper files are created in `VideoIndexer.Tests`.

`MysqlDumpBackupServiceTests.BuildStartInfo_AddsArgumentsAsDiscreteEntries` calls `MysqlDumpBackupService.BuildStartInfo(...)` directly and asserts that host, port, user, password, and database appear as separate entries in `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` (not assembled into a single `Arguments` string).
All 8 new test methods pass with `dotnet test`.

ObfuscationServiceTests.cs was already fully implemented with 12 test methods covering all 5 required behaviors using private nested stub classes (FakeMovieRepository, NullDbConnectionFactory, NullDbConnection, NullDbCommand, NullParameterCollection, NullDataParameter, CollectingProgress).

BackupAsync_ReturnsError_OnNonZeroExitCode uses the DOTNET_HOST_PATH env variable (set by dotnet test) to copy the dotnet.exe host as a fake mysqldump — when invoked with mysqldump-style args it exits non-zero without requiring a real MySQL installation.
All 813 tests pass (6 pre-existing skipped). dotnet build src/VideoIndexer.sln produces 0 warnings, 0 errors.

comments.note: MysqlDumpBackupServiceTests.cs: BackupAsync_ReturnsError_OnNonZeroExitCode copies the dotnet.exe host as a fake mysqldump binary at test runtime. This works reliably in CI (DOTNET_HOST_PATH is set by the test runner) but adds ~200ms to the test due to process startup. A small dedicated stub executable in test assets would be faster and remove the dependency on DOTNET_HOST_PATH.

ObfuscationServiceTests.cs: NullDbConnection, NullDbCommand, NullParameterCollection, NullDataParameter, and the matching NullDbConnectionFactory are per-test-class private stubs that duplicate similar infrastructure already in tests/VideoIndexer.Tests/Fixtures/FakeDbConnectionFactory.cs. Consider consolidating if a third test class needs the same no-op connection stub.
MysqlDumpBackupServiceTests.cs: The summary XML comment still referred only to BuildStartInfo before this WP; it now covers BackupAsync as well. Updated in this implementation.
No observations outside the touched files — all other test infrastructure and source code examined is clean and consistent.

AC-2 confirmed: BuildStartInfo_AddsArgumentsAsDiscreteEntries asserts -h/host, -P/port, -u/username as separate ArgumentList pairs; password as -p<pass> single combined token (mysqldump convention); database as standalone entry; psi.Arguments is empty.

AC-3 confirmed: BackupAsync_ReturnsError_WhenMySqlBinaryFolderNotConfigured constructs service with MySqlBinaryFolder=null, calls BackupAsync, verifies Success=false and ErrorMessage is non-empty. No process spawned.

comments.note: BackupAsync_ReturnsError_OnNonZeroExitCode: null-forgiving operator on Process.GetCurrentProcess().MainModule!.FileName provides a fallback path when DOTNET_HOST_PATH is unset. MainModule is null only under partial-trust execution (not applicable in standard dotnet test runs). Passes reliably on this machine (82 ms).

ObfuscationServiceTests: NullDbConnectionFactory / NullDbConnection / NullDbCommand stubs partially duplicate FakeDbConnectionFactory.cs already present in tests/VideoIndexer.Tests/Fixtures/. This is intentional per AC-1 (inline stubs only) but worth noting if a third test class needs the same no-op DB infrastructure.

MysqlDumpBackupServiceTests.BuildStartInfo_NullConnectionFields_UsesEmptyStrings: asserts Contain("-p") when Password is null. Verifies that a null password produces the "-p" token rather than a NullReferenceException — good defensive coverage.

comments.note: MysqlDumpBackupServiceTests.BuildStartInfo_AddsArgumentsAsDiscreteEntries declares a local `conn` variable with values identical to the class-level `SampleConn` field (Host='db.example.com', Port=3307, etc.). The 'test data locality' pattern is defensible — it keeps expected values visible next to assertions — but without an inline comment the duplication looks accidental. A one-line comment such as '// Explicit values aid injection-safety documentation' would make the intent unambiguous for future contributors.

[documentation-forward] MysqlDumpBackupService.BuildStartInfo accepts an `outputFilePath` parameter that is never used in the method body (stdout streaming is done in BackupAsync, not here). The XML doc comment explains this intent correctly ('Not used internally by this method; provided so unit tests can pass a known path'). Add a note to api-surface.md clarifying this unusual signature so future contributors do not mistake the unused parameter for a bug or attempt to remove it.

summary: Addressed the single documentation-forward from code review: added a MysqlDumpBackupService internal test-accessible method subsection to api-surface.md documenting the BuildStartInfo signature. No README or other documentation gaps were identified — all WP-013 changes were confined to test files (MysqlDumpBackupServiceTests.cs, ObfuscationServiceTests.cs) and required no other documentation updates.
